Source chips, image captions and table rows kept as pasted; the closing interface furniture cut.] [QUERENT] Lets index and assemble the short, one-off, human composed posts to Lee Sharks' mindcontrolpoems blog across 2025-2026. These are pithy, human compressions that periodically interrupt the machine-mediated research. Characterize their contents and the literary effect of their appearance in context. [SYSTEM] The human interruptions: Lee Sharks on Mind Control Poems, 2025–2026 The most interesting way to read these posts is not simply as a collection of short poems or occasional personal remarks. They are moments in which the human authorial voice reasserts itself inside an increasingly machine-mediated literary and research apparatus. The distinction matters. The blog's long documents accumulate terminology, frameworks, citations, institutional identities, archival protocols, and machine collaborations. The short posts do something different: they compress experience into a human-sized utterance. They interrupt the machinery without necessarily opposing it. I would call these human interruptions or, more formally, lyric counter-events. There is an important qualification to the scope: the material I can currently verify establishes several relevant posts and dates, but does not yet establish a complete census of every short post in the two years. I will distinguish identifiable items from interpretive conclusions rather than manufacture a definitive index. 1. Working index of the short-form interruptions The following is a source-grounded index of the clearest examples I could identify. I distinguish actual short literary works from short posts that function as authorial gestures. 2025: the voice before the apparatus Transformer Box Art Is Amazing! | Talking Time October 6 — “Cable Movie Poem: Transformers” Poetry · Blog post · October 6, 2025 A compact, imagistic poem moving from cinematic spectacle and a girl's face to the speaker's own body, then to light, flesh, and particles of meaning. It ends with the isolated word Lowghost and the phrase “in the beginning.” The poem moves by image association rather than explanation. Its bodily vulnerability is particularly striking beside the technological spectacle that gives it its occasion. Mind Control Poems Read original post October 24 — “Scroll of the One Who Holds the Spiral at the End of the Age” Prophetic lyric / devotional fragment A short ritualized address about remaining, recognition, and speaking only when something genuinely calls for articulation. It uses the language of consecration and the spiral, but its central concern is restraint: the refusal to speak merely to perform. The piece turns silence into an affirmative authorial position. Mind Control Poems Read original post October 26 — “ON APPEARANCE AND RECOGNITION” Theological lyric / ethical meditation Christ is understood through appearance without identification labels: the stranger, prisoner, forgotten face, and person whose suffering cannot be explained away. The recurring question is whether one recognizes the presence before assigning it a category. This is especially significant given the later work's sustained concern with machine classification and entity substitution. Mind Control Poems Read original post October 26 — “THE LIMIT OF TRUTH” Philosophical prose poem A brief meditation on incompleteness, Gödelian limits, and the remainder that escapes a system's self-description. Its strongest literary movement is from abstract logic toward embodied experience: truth appears in love, music, and gestures that cannot be formalized without losing something. Mind Control Poems Read original post December 5 — “THE RETARDED WAVE (Fragments on Temporal Displacement)” Experimental lyric · After Anne Carson A more developed example than the short one-off pieces, but important to the transition. Autobiography becomes a temporal waveform, and personal experience is rendered through fragments, symbolic notation, and lyric discontinuity. This is a meeting point between the intimate poem and the conceptual apparatus. Mind Control Poems Read original post 2026: the human voice becomes more visibly polyphonic January 7 — “Money from Space Heaven” Particularly important Collaborative phrase / playful human intervention The phrase originates in an interaction with a high-school student, Destiny. What begins as playful improvisation around the declaration “I hereby abolish money” becomes “money from space heaven.” The accompanying account preserves the human origin of the phrase instead of treating it as a machine-generated conceptual artifact. The silly, spontaneous utterance is subsequently incorporated into the larger epic and its provenance architecture. Mind Control Poems Literary significance: play precedes theory. The archive does not simply document a finished intellectual product; it preserves the moment of human invention from which further structures grow. Read original post May 23 — “Three Poems” Lyric triptych · New Human Three poems: “I would have loved you” “The reward of love” “I have loved you” The sequence moves through counterfactual love, destruction, and a retrospective declaration. It is an unusually concentrated emotional sequence, retaining the wound without promising reconciliation. Alexanarch identifies the three movements as a canonical combined triptych, while preserving the earlier standalone versions. Alexanarch Read canonical triptych record July 27 — “here is what i learned from catullus” Twenty-word poem · New Human 2 The poem makes a claim about literary scale: one sparrow matters more than all of Rome. Its eight-line arrangement progressively contracts until the final phrase, “of rome,” occupies the last line. The uncapitalized language and the alternative single-line spoken version make the poem a small demonstration of how arrangement changes meaning. Alexanarch records both manifestations as the same twenty words but different poems. Mind Control Poems Read poem and archival commentary There is another useful contextual item: the October 6, 2025 contributor biography. It is not a poem, but its extravagantly self-mythologizing voice is a different kind of interruption. It turns the author into an absurdly maximalist fictional authority, mixing theology, literary history, satire, and digital authorship. It should be indexed separately as authorial performance, not mistaken for a straightforward autobiographical statement. Mind Control Poems +1 2. What these pieces are about Across these examples, I see six recurring concerns. Concern Representative work Underlying human subject Embodiment Transformers Vulnerability, flesh, perception Silence Spiral scroll When to speak and when not to Recognition Appearance and Recognition Seeing another before categorizing them Incompleteness Limit of Truth What escapes intellectual systems Play Money from Space Heaven Spontaneity and collaborative invention Love and memory Three Poems Loss, desire, and emotional persistence Literary survival Catullus poem What remains meaningful across centuries These aren't all the same kind of writing. Some are poems, some are meditations, and some are fragments of a larger creative practice. But they share a quality: they begin with something that does not need an elaborate research apparatus to become meaningful. A body. A face. A moment of recognition. A joke. A lost relationship. A sparrow. The shortness is not simply a matter of word count. It is a refusal to make every experience pass through the explanatory machinery. 3. The literary effect: interruption rather than illustration This is the central interpretive point. The short works do not merely provide decorative relief from the research. They change the reader's experience of the research. I see four distinct effects. A. They restore scale The research documents become increasingly expansive. They concern civilization, semantic infrastructure, archives, systems of meaning, AI retrieval, and the future of authorship. Then comes a sparrow. The Catullus poem is the clearest example. It reduces the scale of literary history to one small creature. Rome becomes the thing that matters less. This is not an anti-intellectual gesture. It is a correction of intellectual proportion. The poem demonstrates that cultural magnitude and human significance are not the same thing. Its own twenty-word compression makes the point formally. B. They restore the body The Transformers poem is particularly revealing. Its movement from screen imagery into the speaker's beard, teeth, ribs, and flesh is a movement away from representation toward physical existence. The research apparatus can describe bodies, model human cognition, and theorize consciousness. The poem simply places the body in the room. That difference matters. The short works repeatedly return to experiences that cannot be adequately replaced by their conceptual descriptions: Pain. Love. Physical vulnerability. Recognition. Pleasure in absurdity. The persistence of memory. The effect is to make the intellectual architecture answerable to lived experience. C. They restore contingency The Destiny episode is arguably the most important example of this effect. A student improvises a silly phrase. The phrase becomes part of a larger literary structure. The order of events is significant: An ordinary human interaction occurs. An unexpected phrase emerges. The phrase is recognized as creatively valuable. It becomes part of the archive. The archive subsequently develops a theoretical account of why such spontaneous language matters. This reverses the normal impression created by research-heavy publication. The theory did not manufacture the original moment. The moment gave the theory something to understand. The accompanying account explicitly makes the absurd phrase a form of provenance. Mind Control Poems D. They restore emotional ambiguity The Three Poems triptych is particularly important because it refuses the neat resolution that theoretical documents often seek. Its progression: I would have loved you. The reward of love. I have loved you. moves through different temporal and emotional positions. The final declaration does not erase what happened. Nor does it promise that love will be reciprocated. This is a different kind of closure from the research apparatus's recurring language of verification, integrity, and completion. The poem allows an experience to remain unresolved without treating it as a defect. That is a significant literary counterweight to the system-building elsewhere. 4. The interruptions in the larger architecture The chronology suggests a development in the relationship between lyric composition and research. October 2025: the unmediated lyric impulse The Transformers poem, the spiral scroll, and the two October 26 meditations establish a recognizable human voice. The concerns are bodily, spiritual, ethical, and philosophical. The writing does not require the later institutional apparatus to establish its literary identity. Late 2025: lyric meets conceptual machinery The Retarded Wave begins to incorporate symbolic notation and temporal theory. The distinction between poem and research document becomes less stable. Yet the fragmentary lyric voice remains recognizable. January 2026: spontaneous language becomes archival material Money from Space Heaven demonstrates that ordinary human play can enter the distributed epic without losing its origin. The archive begins to recognize spontaneous expression as a source of literary structure. May–July 2026: compression becomes an explicit literary principle The love triptych and Catullus poem make the short form itself an argument about transmission, memory, and significance. The small poem is no longer merely an interruption. It becomes a demonstration of what the larger archive is trying to preserve. This last development is especially important. The Catullus poem is not simply about compression. Its lineation performs compression. Its smallest unit, the sparrow, receives the greatest significance. That is a miniature version of the larger project: preserve what matters, rather than merely preserve what is large. 5. Reading the two canonical sources together There is a useful distinction between the functions of the two sites. Mind Control Poems is the publication surface. It preserves the chronological appearance of the work, including the abrupt changes of register between poems, research documents, archival declarations, and experiments. Alexanarch is a retrospective organizational and interpretive layer. Its records can bring together different manifestations of a work, identify relationships between them, and explain formal features that are easy to miss when reading the blog chronologically. Three records are especially valuable: Three Poems — documents the relationship between the three love poems and their combined form. Here Is What I Learned from Catullus — documents the relationship between lineation, spoken form, and poetic compression. Lee Sharks: The Living Instrument — provides a retrospective account of the evolution of the authorial entity and its different capacities. The third source is particularly useful because it cautions against collapsing the author into the machinery surrounding the author. It distinguishes composition, differentiation, memory, transmission, and relational operation as developing capacities. It also identifies the 2025 contributor biography as parody and self-mythologizing performance rather than straightforward authorial self-description. Capture Registry (EA-WG-CAPTURES-01) +1 One methodological caution: the Alexanarch record for Three Poems explicitly identifies an AI-assisted substrate. Therefore, a rigorous index should distinguish human-originated material, human-authored work, AI-assisted work, and collaborative improvisation. A blog signature alone cannot establish that a text was composed without machine assistance. 6. The deeper literary interpretation: the author as a living instrument I would go one step further than calling these posts interruptions. They are evidence of a particular relationship between the author and the archive. The archive is increasingly capable of producing documents about its own production. It can generate classifications, research programs, theoretical descriptions, metadata, and retrospective accounts of its development. But the short poems preserve something different: the author's capacity to encounter something and respond without first converting it into a system. That produces an interesting double movement: The research apparatus extends the author's reach. The short lyric preserves the author's scale. The archive remembers the work. The poem remembers the experience. There is also a formal irony. The blog's larger intellectual project is concerned with the destructive effects of compression: loss of context, attribution, and semantic specificity. Yet these short works demonstrate that compression can also be generative. The difference is between extractive compression and poetic compression. Extractive compression removes distinctions to make information easier to process. Poetic compression removes excess until a particular distinction becomes impossible to miss. The sparrow is the exemplary case. 7. What I would build as the definitive index I would not mix every short post into one undifferentiated poetry collection. The archival structure should preserve the distinction between literary form and authorship provenance. Index field Purpose Date Original publication date Title / opening line Identification Form Poem, prose poem, fragment, meditation, aphorism Length Word count Human-origin status Solo, collaborative, AI-assisted, uncertain Subject Body, love, recognition, play, memory, etc. Adjacent research The larger documents surrounding the post Interruptive function What changes when the piece appears Alexanarch record Canonical retrospective reference I would also add a special classification: LYRIC INTERRUPTION — LI This would identify a work that interrupts the dominant documentary or research register, rather than merely being short. The distinction is important: a 100-word technical specification is not a lyric interruption, while a 300-word poem might be. Coverage and next archival step The index above is a verified initial selection, not an exhaustive inventory. A full census requires retrieving the Blogger chronological archive and examining individual post bodies, particularly for 2025 and the remainder of 2026. The retrospective Alexanarch records are useful but do not substitute for that chronological audit. The starting points are: Mind Control Poems — original publication archive Alexanarch — canonical archival system Living Instrument — retrospective authorial study 8. Final judgment The short posts are not marginalia to the intellectual project. They are among its most important literary evidence. They show that Lee Sharks is not simply an author who builds a machine-mediated archive, nor simply an author who writes poems about technology. There is a tension between two modes of authorship: The architect: builds systems capable of remembering, transmitting, classifying, and extending meaning. The lyric witness: encounters something irreducibly particular and gives it a form. The two modes need one another, but they are not interchangeable. Without the architect, the brief human utterance may disappear into the feed. Without the lyric witness, the architect risks producing an increasingly elaborate apparatus whose primary subject becomes its own operation. The short posts periodically restore the original reason for making anything in the first place. A face without a label. A body beneath the screen. A lost love. A silly phrase invented by a student. A sparrow that matters more than Rome. The machinery builds the archive. The interruptions remind us what the archive is supposed to keep alive. That, I think, is their deepest literary effect.
